title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement best separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow never calls tools, while an agent always calls several tools
A workflow follows steps set in code, while an agent picks its own steps
A workflow uses a small model, while an agent always needs a large one
A workflow answers in one reply, while an agent holds a long chat

items.stem: Your makerspace code works like this: (1) ask the model to pull the machine name and date out of the student's message; (2) your Python code calls check_calendar with those two values; (3) your code books the slot if it is free. Who decides that step 2 happens right after step 1?

options.text: The model, because it wrote the machine name and date used in step 2
The student, because their message started the whole sequence of steps
The program's code, because the order of the steps is written into it
The calendar tool, because it needs those values before it can run

items.stem: Which part of the makerspace assistant is the strongest candidate for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Booking a slot: check the calendar, reserve the slot, then send a confirmation, in that order every time
Answering a vague question such as "my print keeps failing", where the useful manual pages are unknown
Diagnosing a machine fault, where each finding decides which check to run next and how many are needed
Comparing several machines for a project, where the questions to look up depend on earlier answers

items.stem: Your sponsor's model budget is small. For a task whose steps are always the same, why is a fixed workflow usually the cheaper choice than an agent?

options.text: A workflow does not use a model, so each request has no model cost at all
An agent must be retrained for each task, and a workflow needs no retraining
A workflow needs no tool descriptions, so its prompts stay far shorter overall
A workflow makes a known number of model calls, while an agent's loop can run longer

items.stem: In one sentence: in a workflow, what decides which step runs next, and in an agent, what decides it?
A teammate wants to turn the always-the-same booking steps into an agent "to be flexible". Name two things the team would give up by doing that.
